name: Cocoa-nut Jumbles
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Rub half a pound of butter into a pound of sifted flour.
Wet it with three beaten eggs and a little rose water.
Add by degrees the cocoa-nut, so as to form a stiff dough.
Flour your hands and your paste-board.
Divide the dough into equal portions and make the jumbles with your hands into long rolls.
Curl them round and join the ends so as to form rings.
Lay them in buttered pans, not so near as to run into each other.
Bake them in a quick oven from five to ten minutes.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Grate a large cocoa-nut.
2. Rub half a pound of butter into a pound of sifted flour.
3. Wet it with three beaten eggs and a little rose water.
4. Add by degrees the cocoa-nut, so as to form a stiff dough.
5. Flour your hands and your paste-board.
6. Divide the dough into equal portions and make the jumbles with your hands into long rolls.
7. Curl them round and join the ends so as to form rings.
8. Grate loaf-sugar over them.
9. Lay them in buttered pans, not so near as to run into each other.
10. Bake them in a quick oven from five to ten minutes.
